note:
The manifest of every external input to this tree, code and data alike. Nothing enters the tree undeclared (plan L0 step 3). Entries are pinned by URL and SHA-256, never by version range, because rule R11 applies to code for the same reason it applies to data: upstream is mutable and a resolver hides that. See MANIFEST.md for the format.

ARCHIVES DECLARE WHAT IS TAKEN OUT OF THEM. An archive's SHA-256 pins the container and says nothing about which of its members this tree reads. Every entry with `unpack` therefore carries `consumes` — `whole-tree` where the archive is compiled entire, `declared-members` where it is not — and a `members` list giving each individually-read member its own SHA-256: the licence text quoted verbatim into NOTICE, the file compared against a populated FetchContent tree, or a data member extracted into the cache because something outside Python needs a path to it. tools/fetch.py refuses an archive entry that declares neither. The rule was prompted by EGM2008, which ships seven members of which this tree reads two and deliberately does not open hsynth_WGS84.f, and it applies to every archive rather than to the one that revealed it.

entries.role: JPL DE440 planetary and lunar ephemeris, WITH the TT-TDB time ephemeris — the full-span kernel, and the only independent check of tdb_minus_tt in this tree

SUBSTITUTED FOR de440.bsp on 2026-09-18, not added alongside it, and the substitution was verified rather than assumed: reading both DAFs' segment summaries directly, de440t.bsp carries de440.bsp's 14 segments with IDENTICAL frame, type and span, plus ONE more — target 1000000001 about centre 1000000000, the TT-TDB time ephemeris. Nothing that consumed de440.bsp loses anything.
WHY: accuracy is not the argument. At 1 microsecond of TDB-TT error, ten times any error credibly attributed to the analytic series, the Sun's geocentric position moves 30 mm and the third-body acceleration by about 3.5e-15 m/s^2, which nothing in this tree can see. The argument is that tdb_minus_tt otherwise has NO independent check anywhere, and the failure it is exposed to is not a 100 ns failure but a wrapping, unit or sign failure: 1 ms puts the Sun 30 m out and the Moon 1 m out, and that is visible everywhere.
NOTE THE HOST: de440t.bsp is published by JPL SSD, not by NAIF. NAIF's generic_kernels/spk/planets/ carries de440, de440s, de441 and de442 and NO de440t, and the obvious URL there is a 404.

entries.role: Fehlberg, NASA TR R-287 (1968) — RK7(8) and RK8(9) coefficients (Tables X, XII), the truncation-error term (134), and Example (53) with its closed-form exact solution and published accumulated errors (Tables XI, XIII). SPEC-integrators, L3 step 2.
entries.licence_note: NASA technical report, public domain.
entries.verify_note: THIS IS A 1968 SCAN AND ITS OCR IS UNUSABLE FOR THE MATHEMATICS. pdftotext renders Table X's beta block as '83_ = 841 = B_I = 8sl = B71 = Be1', and mangles even the contents page ('TABLE IN.' for III, 'SectionXVHI' for XVIII, '8O' for 80) -- the I/1 and O/0 confusions that matter most for digits. THE PAGE IMAGES ARE PERFECTLY LEGIBLE: rendered at 150 dpi, Table X (report p.65, PDF p.72) gives the coefficients as EXACT RATIONALS -- alpha = 0, 2/27, 1/9, 1/6, 5/12, 1/2, 5/6, 1/6, 2/3, 1/3, 1, 0, 1; c = 41/840, 34/105, 9/35, 9/280; TE = (41/840)(f0 + f10 - f11 - f12)h at (134). So the coefficients must be read from the IMAGES, not the text layer -- and, crucially, the transcription is then verified against the RUNGE-KUTTA ORDER CONDITIONS, which are exact algebraic identities independent of the scan. A misread digit fails them. The source's legibility is therefore not what the gate rests on.

entries.role: Burns, J. A., Lamy, P. L., Soter, S. (1979), 'Radiation forces on small particles in the solar system', Icarus 40:1-48. The classic first-order (v/c) statement of aberration and Poynting-Robertson drag, Eq. (5): m*dv/dt = (S*A/c)*Q_pr*[(1 - rdot/c)*S_hat - v/c] -- the radial Doppler factor plus the drag term, with Q_pr the radiation-pressure efficiency (1 for a perfect absorber; Q_abs + Q_sca for an isotropic scatterer; up to 2*Q for a particle that perfectly backscatters, which a flat specular reflector near normal incidence approaches). L4 step 5's SRP plugin aberration term (PHPR-R-010).

entries.role: Kezerashvili, R. Ya., Vazquez-Poritz, J. F. (2010), 'The Poynting-Robertson Effect on Solar Sails', arXiv:1012.3574. An independent derivation of the aberration/PR-drag force for a solar sail directly facing the Sun (pitch angle zero -- the same geometry a sun-tracking panel always has), Eq. (4)-(6): reflected and absorbed contributions each carrying the aberration angle alpha = sin^-1(v_phi/c) separately, rather than one lumped Q_pr. Cross-checks BLS79's own normal-incidence case for a partially-reflective (not perfectly absorbing or perfectly specular) surface; does not extend to oblique incidence either, so it does not close the flat-plate generalisation's own open bound (PHPR-R-010). L4 step 5.
